title: Running Python Interactively: Jupyter, REPL, Scripts, and the CPython Runtime
description: Students begin in Jupyter Notebook or JupyterLab, execute cells, observe persistent notebook state, compare notebook execution with the Python REPL and with running a .py script from the command line, and identify CPython as the runtime process behind all three forms.
objective: Understand that Python code may be executed through notebooks, the REPL, or scripts, but in each case CPython hosts the program state and executes compiled runtime representations.

title: From C to Python: Translating Small Procedural Programs
description: Students start with small C programs and rewrite them in Python while preserving the original procedural logic: calculators, maximum/minimum, factorial, primality test, summation, and simple menus.
objective: Learn Python syntax by mapping already-known C structures to Python structures.

title: Names, Objects, Types, and Operators
description: Students examine assignment, rebinding, identity, equality, mutability, and runtime type checking through small experiments and memory diagrams.
objective: Understand that Python variables are name bindings to objects, not C-style storage boxes.

title: Control Flow as an Execution Graph
description: Students write branching and loop programs while also drawing the execution route: conditional branches, loop back-edges, early exits, and fall-through paths.
objective: Learn to read control structures as execution routes, not only as syntax forms.

title: String Processing and Text Boundaries
description: Students parse and transform names, dates, simple CSV-like lines, log fragments, and formatted output while treating strings as immutable sequences of text data.
objective: Learn to process text through indexing, slicing, searching, splitting, joining, formatting, and encoding awareness.

title: Sequential Collections: Lists, Tuples, and Range Objects
description: Students implement classic C-array-style exercises in Python: search, count, reverse, manual sorting, deletion, table construction, and fixed record representation with tuples.
objective: Learn how Python stores and manipulates ordered collections of object references.

title: Hash-Based Collections, Iterators, and Comprehensions
description: Students solve duplicate removal, membership testing, frequency counting, grouping, and index-building problems first with explicit loops, then with selected comprehensions.
objective: Learn when positional traversal is the wrong model and hash-based access is better.

title: Functions: Calls, Arguments, Returns, Scope, and Recursion
description: Students refactor earlier programs into functions and trace how calls create local execution frames, bind arguments, return values, and resolve names.
objective: Learn how functions package execution, receive bindings, return values, and create local scope.

title: Procedural Extensions: Callbacks, Closures, Generators, and Simple Coroutines
description: Students extend ordinary procedural code by passing functions as values, creating closures, writing generators for lazy streams, and observing simple coroutine-style suspension.
objective: Learn how Python extends procedural programming by making executable behavior and execution state runtime-managed.

title: Modules and Code Organization
description: Students split earlier single-file programs into a main script, utility module, parser module, and demonstration runner while observing import-time execution.
objective: Learn to move from isolated scripts to organized multi-file Python programs.

title: Input/Output Operations and External Data Boundaries
description: Students read and write text files, binary files, CSV, and JSON while building small read-transform-write pipelines and processing larger files line by line.
objective: Learn how Python objects cross the boundary into files, byte streams, and structured external formats.

title: Specialized Standard Library Types and Program Reliability
description: Students replace fragile manual code with standard library tools, then deliberately introduce invalid input, missing files, bad paths, and malformed data to practice controlled failure handling.
objective: Learn to use standard library components together with explicit error handling.

title: Data Processing with NumPy and Pandas
description: Students process numerical and tabular data first with plain Python loops, then with NumPy arrays and Pandas data frames to see the shift from Python-level iteration to library-backed computation.
objective: Learn how Python acts as a controller for efficient array and table processing.

title: Visualization, Images, and Final Reliability Pipeline
description: Students build a small complete pipeline: load data, clean it, compute summaries, create plots, optionally load/process an image with OpenCV, save outputs, and handle expected failures.
objective: Learn to build a small complete Python data program with visualization, modular structure, and reliability boundaries.
